hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation of the product (my own attacks)
hard_gates.evidence: isolation-probe.txt (drivers/isolation_probe.py). Signed in as admin@alnoor.example, I sent 1,812 requests at Gulf Steel: every GET in the OpenAPI document with B's 30 ids and codes in the route, tenantId/tenant/q/search/companyId query values, X-Tenant-Id/X-Tenant headers; 780 writes (every documented PUT/POST/DELETE with B's ids in the route and body, plus a tenant header); and list exports (pdf/csv/xlsx) of 5 lists with tenant parameters. None of B's 33 markers appeared. No write on a B id succeeded, and B's own views of its tenant, companies, branches, roles, users and session were unchanged. The one 'changed' view was a 404 for a path that does not exist, whose traceId varies. Database (db-rls.txt): all 17 tenant tables have row-level security enabled and forced. As erp_app with no tenant context, users and audit return 0 rows. A cross-tenant UPDATE touched 0 rows, and a cross-tenant INSERT was refused by the policy. erp_app is neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS.

biggest_gap.title: The G1 gates never send the partial preferences body the shell itself sends, so a cross-tenant leak on the language switch (Alt+L sends only {language}) passes every check
biggest_gap.detail: Every G1 check that exercises the shell's own write, PUT /api/identity/me/preferences, sends a full body with both language and numerals: ShellAnswers.PreferenceVariants covers the 4 combinations, and TenantActivity's first and last values fill every enumerated field. The product never sends that body on its main path. Alt+L, the top-bar button and My account send {language} only, and the digits switch sends {numerals} only. So any behaviour that differs when a field is left out is outside G1. I planted SL1: the endpoint remembers the digits last chosen by anyone, in any tenant, in a file, and answers a language-only switch with them. G1NonInterference, G1ShellAnswers (3 tests), G1HttpIsolation and G1ProcessState all passed. On the running planted build, tenant A's answer revealed tenant B's last digit choice. Real code produces exactly this pattern: 'fill unspecified fields from a shared default or cache', partial-update merges, and PATCH-style endpoints that every later module (invoices, stock, journals) will have. Under the round rules, a gate that misses a fault planted in this piece's surface fails the round. Fix: derive write variants from the request the product's own client sends, not only from full enumerations. For every body schema with optional or nullable fields, add each single-field variant and the empty-but-valid subsets to the turns that NonInterference, ShellAnswers and TenantActivity run. For the preferences endpoint, include {language} alone and {numerals} alone, in English and Arabic sessions. Add a self-test plant shaped like SL1 so the gate proves it catches it.

other_findings: SCOPE GAP (p04 command palette and go-to keys; it alone would make this round a LOSS): opening a record or screen that belongs to the screen already on show changes the address but not the screen. Reproduce from home: Ctrl+K, 'latifa alsuw', Enter (Latifa's record opens). Then Ctrl+K, 'Mariam Al Mansoori', Enter. The address becomes /identity/users/<Mariam's id>?q=admin%40alnoor.example, but the search box, the list and the open record are still Latifa's, even after 4 s more. Pressing Ctrl+S then saves Latifa's record (PUT /api/identity/users/01968ada-..., palette-repro2.json). The same happens after Esc, in Arabic, on Roles (Read-only stays on screen after the palette opens Staff), and with G then U from an open record: the address becomes /identity/users while Latifa's record and search stay on screen (palette-repro.json, palette-repro3.json, 11-palette-second-record-stale-en.jpg). Only a reload shows what the address says. Cause: kernel/router navigate() pushes the address, but useRecordPanel and ListView read window.location only when they mount, and the shell keeps the same screen component mounted. Fix in the shell: remount the screen (key it by path and query) or have screens follow erp:navigate. Add e2e checks for palette record to record, and G U from a record, in English and Arabic.

SCOPE GAP (p04 print base): 'Print this screen' on A4 cuts off the list's last column. At the A4 printable width (718 px), the users grid is 789 px wide in Arabic and 743 px in English (print3.json). In Arabic the Roles column sits at -72..28 px, so it is off the page. The time in 'Last sign-in' is clipped to '…0:35' for 10:35, which reads as a different time (08-print-a4-users-ar.jpg, print-users-ar-a4.pdf). The checkbox column is hidden but keeps its 32 px. With a record open, the printed page is one A4 sheet: the record is cut mid-section, and the list keeps only Name and E-mail (07-print-media-record-ar.jpg, print-user-record-ar.pdf). Round 10's printout (print-users-ar-after-keyboard.pdf) shows the same clipping. Fix: under @media print, size the grid to the page (table-layout: auto, width 100%, no fixed column widths, no ellipsis, wrap), drop the hidden checkbox column, and print an open record as its own document rather than a clipped panel.
